sentences.text: Priya Nandra is a social worker from adult social care.
The assessment is a review following Edna Hollis's fall in October.
The purpose of the visit is to assess how carers are working out after the fall.
Edna Hollis is present during the meeting.
The person uses a frame in the house due to hip stiffness.
Edna Hollis does not go out without someone accompanying her.
Carers visit in the morning and at teatime.
The morning carer is named Jade.
Jade helps with medication and personal washing.
Teatime calls are described as 'a bit quick sometimes' with carers coming in and out.
Carers provide tea at teatime.
Edna Hollis's daughter Sandra shops for her on a Saturday when she can.
Sandra lives in Castleford and drives to the shop.
Edna Hollis's grandson Kyle visits most weeks.
Kyle brings paper and goes to the cash machine for Edna.
Kyle uses Edna's bank card to access money.
Edna gave Kyle her bank card number, as it is easier.
Kyle takes out £50 per week from the bank card for himself.
Edna did not agree to Kyle taking £50 per week; she did not consent to this arrangement.
Edna does not want Kyle to be involved in police action or legal proceedings.
Edna wants her money to be hers and does not want it taken by Kyle.
Kyle took £400 from Edna's purse for Christmas presents three weeks ago.
The £400 was in Edna's purse and went missing after Kyle visited.
Kyle said he would repay the £400, and Edna believes this is not theft but a loan.
Edna does not know if Kyle gambles, as she has not seen it.
Sandra told Edna that Kyle gambles on his phone through betting apps.
Edna has not seen Kyle gambling, and does not know about the gambling activity.
Sandra knows about the £400 in the purse but not about the bank card use.
Edna does not believe Kyle has threatened or hurt her.
The social worker will log a safeguarding concern due to money being taken by Kyle.
